sermon.title: Hope in Disasters
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts, forgives, and promises to do us good. He then lays out our part, to repent, believe the gospel, confess Jesus as Lord and receive Him, and uses the butterfly and 1 John 2 to describe growing from baby to child to young man to father in Christ.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he names Jeremiah 32:9 and 32:39 for the words “one heart and one way” and “rejoice over them to do them good”; those words are in Jeremiah 32:39 and 32:41. He says Hebrews 8 “adds” that God will be “a God of supernatural power”; the NKJV of Hebrews 8:10 reads “I will be their God,” so the phrase is his own explanation. Two names of Judah’s kings and the name of a reformer in his list of preachers (about 1:39, 1:51 and 4:50) were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear].

chunks.section_question: What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?
chunks.short_answer: He says Josiah was the last good king, but his son “burned the Scriptures” and did evil before God, the first captivity came, and later the king of Babylon burned Jerusalem and destroyed the temple. He says Jeremiah 32 was written about ten years after that, and asks, “If Israel had hope, do we have hope?”
chunks.text:
Okay, we’re going to go to Jeremiah chapter 31 and 32, but we want you to understand and remember when these chapters were written. Okay? You remember a few lessons ago we showed you that Josiah was the last good king of Israel. All right, looks like Israel was going to avoid the captivity and everything, because Josiah really turned to God, got the nation to turn to God, reinstituted the feast and the things of God. But then his son came on the throne. How many of you had children that didn’t follow your ways? Jehoiakim came up. He reigned 11 years, and he burned the Scriptures, just burned them, and he did evil before God. He shed innocent blood. He committed abominations. Abominations is sexual immorality, homosexuality, idolatry, stealing, murder. In Proverbs 6:17, you remember, there’s seven things

that the Lord, it’s called abominations: a lying tongue, a proud look, hands that shed innocent blood, he that devises wicked imaginations, feet that are swift to running to do evil, a false witness that repeats lies and speaks lies, and he that sows division among the brethren, and there’s many others. Okay? And he committed them. He committed them all. All right, he had wars, there were famine, there were plagues, and the first captivity came at the end of his term. Then [unclear] arose, and he was king, made king by the king of Babylon, and he only lasted three months, but the Bible just summed him up and said he did evil like [unclear] did. Now it was in this condition that chapter 31 was written.

Hallelujah. I mean, we got serious calamity. America’s got calamities, but nothing this bad yet. So if Israel had hope, do we have hope? If Israel would have listened to Jeremiah, 31 and 32 could have saved them a lot of pain, and so can we. Hallelujah. Then we go down to Zedekiah. He reigned 11 years, and the second captivity came in the 11th year, and this time the king of Babylon destroyed and burned the city of Jerusalem, destroyed the temple. He imprisoned the preacher of righteousness, Jeremiah, and this is when Jeremiah 32 was written, okay, about 10 years later.

chunks.section_question: What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)
chunks.short_answer: He says “a covenant is a contract,” like promising a lender to pay for a house: each side does its part. Of the new covenant he says, “this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part,” and that God does it, not any preacher.
chunks.text:
Now you got the picture. Things are really bad here, and the people keep being bad, they keep rejecting, and God keeps giving them hope. And this is what God says as we’re coming up. Remember, the false prophets are still prophesying falsely. How many of you know we got false prophets today, false teachers teaching their own doctrine? Temple leaders, the citizens, his own hometown tried to kill Jeremiah, tried to silence the Word of God. Everybody’s wanting to kill Jeremiah. The temple leaders tried to kill him, imprison him. And if you’re going to stand up for right, people are going to dislike you, and that’s one of the reasons we don’t stand up for right, is we don’t want people not liking us. Jeremiah 31:31: “The days come.” Here’s God talking in the midst of this, and watch, this is really simple.

It’s just plain, clear English. This is what God says: “I will make a new covenant,” a fresh covenant, a fresh contract, “with Israel and Judah.” A covenant is a contract. If I go to buy a house, I promise the lender that I will pay the payments, I promise the government that I will pay the taxes, and they let me buy that house, live in it. If I don’t pay the payments or I don’t pay the taxes, they kick me out. See, they do their part, I have to do my part. So this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part. This is what God says, this is what I will do. Who will do it? God. Not the Pope, not Billy Graham, not Martin Luther, not [unclear].

chunks.section_question: Will everyone in the new covenant know God, keep His commandments, and be forgiven? (Jeremiah 31:33-34)
chunks.short_answer: He says God promises to put His law in the inward part, our spirit, and that “all shall know Me, from the least to the greatest,” which he ties to knowing God personally (John 17:3) and keeping His commandments. He says God also forgives the iniquity and will “remember your sin no more,” and asks, “If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves?”
chunks.text:
God says, “I’ll do this.” And how many would rather have God than any preacher that we’ve ever heard? Yes. “I will put My law in their inward parts and in their heart.” The inward part is that third part of us, that spirit. All of us have a spirit within us, and He says He’s going to put His Word in that spiritual man, that spirit man that’s in you, and in your mind: “I’ll put My law, I’ll put My Word in there.” And if He doesn’t, you don’t know nothing. Can I hear an amen? And He says, “I’ll do this.” I’ll do this next: “All shall know Me, from the least to the greatest.” All shall know Me. All right, as we’ve taught you before, the Bible says in John 17:3 that this is eternal life, that they may know God the Father and Jesus Christ His Son. Have a relationship with Him, a personal relationship.

All right, a personal encounter. But not only that, it says in First John that we know that we know Him if we keep His commandments. See, all will know Me, all will keep My commandments, all will have a relationship with Me. Hallelujah, that’s powerful. From the least to the greatest, no matter how little you think you are, no matter how puny of a Christian you think you are, God says you’ll know Me, and you’ll keep My Word, to the greatest. Hallelujah. That’s your promise. Can God lie? No. All right, next: “I will forgive your iniquity,” your immoral, immorality I should say, and the punishment for immorality. You see, I will forgive it. The breaking of moral laws comes with a punishment. He said, “I’ll forgive it, I’ll render it zero, I’ll look at it like it never happened, and I will remember your sin no more.” And if God forgets our sin, shouldn’t we? Yeah, you got to. If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves? Yes. If God erases the sin and doesn’t bring it up again, shouldn’t we? Yeah. Hallelujah. Very powerful, very powerful.

chunks.section_question: What does the covenant mean by “one heart and one way,” and what is the fear of the Lord? (Hebrews 8; Jeremiah 32)
chunks.short_answer: He says Hebrews 8 repeats the covenant and adds that God will be “a God of supernatural power,” doing what humans can’t do. He says God promises “one heart and one way,” that “there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that the fear of the Lord is to “depart from evil and hate evil.”
chunks.text:
“I will be to them,” now Hebrews 8 repeats this in the New Testament, repeats it word by word, but adds this: “I will be to them a God of supernatural power, and they shall be My people.” Who needs a supernatural power? Hallelujah. I’ll do things that humans can’t do, “and they who come into covenant with Me, they will be My people.” Well, I like that. If God before us, who can stand against us? Amen. God’s on my side, even when I’m the least. Even when I’m the least, He’s on my side. He’s not going to keep me, the flea on the dog. Jeremiah 32:9: “I will give them one heart and one way.” One heart, one way. We got all these denominational Protestant churches and everybody thinks their little camp is the best.

That Paul plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church. Amen. We got to get rid of these tags, and all of us have to line up to that. God, putting a name on your church building and saying, “Well, we believe this,” doesn’t count. All of us have the responsibility to line up to Him. I don’t care what the tag is out on your church. And He says, “I’m going to do that.” Do we need this one answered in America? Amen, and throughout the world, “that they may fear Me forever.” For how long? Forever. What is the fear of the Lord? Depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord. He said, “I will give you one heart and one way.” Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” He is the way. No man comes to the Father but by Me. All right, and He says, “I’ll do this so that you fear Me, you hate evil, and you depart from evil, and I’ll do this for the good of them and their children.”

chunks.section_question: Why does God want to do you good, and will He ever turn away from you? (Jeremiah 32:40)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the whole thing is to do you good,” so that your neighbor sees God’s blessing, and that this is the last covenant: “there ain’t no other covenant coming.” He says God will not turn away from you “even in your despair, even in your stupidity and your rebellion,” and, like the prodigal son, you can remember the father’s house and go back.
chunks.text:
See, the whole thing is to do you good. And the reason God wants to do you good is because the world looks at success. They measure everything by success. And so if God can get you to obey His covenant, He’s going to make you good. He’s going to bless your finances, bless your health, He’s going to bless your life. Why? Because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor, that they see it pays to what? Serve God. Now, “I will make an everlasting covenant with them.” So is there another covenant coming after this one? No. This is the what? Everlasting. There was the Adamic covenant, God’s covenant with Adam. There was the Noah covenant, God’s covenant with Noah. There was the David covenant, God’s covenant with David. There was the Moses covenant, God’s covenant with His people Israel. And now He says, “I’m going to bring in the last covenant, and it’s going to be forever.” So there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one. We don’t need another one. See that? “I will not turn away from them.” Man, that is so encouraging. How many of you ever just really messed up, to where you thought God didn’t hear you anymore, didn’t even like you anymore? Yeah. Well, the covenant says He will what? Not turn away from you, even in your despair, even in your stupidity and your rebellion. He’s going to be drawing you back to Him to

bless you and do you good. And if you are like the prodigal son and you wake up in the pigpen, just remember what the father said. That’s what the prodigal son did. He remembered what the father said. He remembered what the house of the father was, and he went back to the house, back to the father, and the father restored it. And that’s exactly what God said He would do in this covenant. So never let Satan or people around you talk you into giving up. God is for you. And again, He won’t turn away from you, because He wants to do you good. “I will put My fear in their hearts.” There it is again: My fear in their hearts, I’ll do it. “And they shall not depart from Me.” You know, from the day I got saved, backsliding and going back to the world was never even a temptation with me, because I really met God, I really had a born again experience. “They shall not depart from Me.” Wow, I love it.

chunks.section_question: Does God bring or allow calamity to correct His people? (Jeremiah 32:39-42)
chunks.short_answer: He says nothing can separate us from God’s love, and that God is “out to do you good,” using the word “good” four times. He says God allowed plague, famine and conquest to correct Israel because “if He didn’t allow it, Satan can’t do anything, and nations can’t do anything,” but that if they return to the covenant He will “bring all the good upon them.”
chunks.text:
See, nothing can separate us, Paul said, from the love of God which is in Christ. Nothing: principalities or powers, things to come, things behind, things here present, nothing. Jeremiah 32:39: “I will rejoice over them to do them good.” Here’s that word “good” again. That’s three times God’s out to do you good. Don’t you listen to this world, because God does you good. “I will plant them in this land.” His kingdom, His kingdom of righteousness, peace, and joy. His kingdom is what we enter into, and He said He will plant us. “Like as I have brought this great evil upon these people.” See, God corrected them. God brought, or allowed Satan to come and plague them with plagues, and the king of Babylon to conquer them in war. You see, famine, He allowed the famine to happen, because if He didn’t allow it, Satan can’t do anything, and nations can’t do anything. He’s the Lord of it all.

“So will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised.” There’s that word “good” again. That’s four times. Is God wanting to do you good? Yeah, we get the hint. Following Him, you will wind up with a good life, I guarantee you. God will come and correct us, and God will allow your sins and your rebellion to bring corrections in your life. The Bible says their sin will correct them. Sin has a punishment, sin has a correction. You see, but He says if I do that, I will also what? Bring all the good upon them. All they got to do is get back to My covenant and I will forget all of that stuff and bless them again. Now that’s powerful, and it’s very clear, very clear. As you see the development of a butterfly here, is our part. This is our part, this is what we got to do. People say, “Not by works.” I’m sorry, not by works of the ceremonial shadow laws of the Bible, but you’ve got to apply the spiritual laws to get the spiritual answers. Are you with me?

chunks.section_question: What is our part in the covenant: repent and believe the gospel? (Mark 1:15; Luke 13:5; 1 John 1:9)
chunks.short_answer: He says “this is our part”: repent, turn from your evil ways, leave sin behind and “believe the gospel,” trusting God the way astronauts trusted their spaceship. Citing Luke 13:5, he says our trust has to be in Jesus, “not a church, not a pastor, not our own opinions,” and that we must admit with our mouth that we were wrong so He forgives and cleanses.
chunks.text:
So this is what you got to do. This is what you got to put an effort in. Mark chapter 1:15: “Repent.” See, repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways. You got to turn, you got to leave sin behind, the drugs, all that stuff that Satan puts out there to try to lure you. You got to turn from it and “believe the gospel.” So you got to put your trust in the gospel. These astronauts that went into space to go to the moon, they had to trust that spaceship, the engineers that built it, the mechanics that put it together, the architects that drew it, and the scientists that studied all the laws that hindered them from getting into space and how to overcome. chunks.section_question: What does the butterfly teach about growing as a Christian, and what is a “baby” in Christ? (1 John 2:12)
chunks.short_answer: He says God gave us a covenant “to make us like Himself,” so “we can’t be satisfied with staying where we’re at.” Using 1 John 2, he says babies are those whose sins are forgiven but who still have habitual sin, like the egg and caterpillar, and the church should understand what stage they are in and “keep feeding them, keep nourishing them.”
chunks.text:
metamorphosis, the changing from the egg to the cocoon to the beautiful butterfly that lays the egg, and it starts all over again. Hallelujah. And this is the message the American church has got to get. We can’t be satisfied with staying where we’re at when God has given us a covenant to make us like Himself and to do us good. 1 John 2:12 and 14 plainly lays it out to us. Babies. See, he talks about the babies: “Your sins are forgiven.” He tells us who babies are: your sins are forgiven. That’s it. And my sins are forgiven. They may have still, and most of them do have, habitual sin still in their life. See, this is the egg to the caterpillar.

That caterpillar comes out and eats the egg. It goes back, turns back. You’ll see him, if you had have seen it, he crawled out and then he went back to that egg, that old life, and he partook of it. And this is what baby Christians do. They have habitual sins still in their life, and so that’s babies. So babies, when they’re making mistakes, church, understand what stage they’re in and keep feeding them, keep nourishing them, so they overcome these things. Amen. They grow. And then you got Christians that are 15 years old and claim to be mature, and they have habitual sins. How many of you know that’s not maturity at all? That is still baby level. They haven’t grown up. Remember, it only took three years for the tree in the Bible to produce fruit. This isn’t, you know, a lifetime thing. God said He would do a quick work.

chunks.section_question: What is a spiritual “father” in Christ, and why must Jesus be Lord and Teacher, not only Savior?
chunks.short_answer: He says fathers know Jesus from the beginning of the Bible to the end, love Him, and “can birth others” through the gospel, while “children can’t birth.” He says too many rely on the Savior stage, but “we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord.”
chunks.text:
You know the Bible and you overcome the wicked one. He can’t tempt you, test you, lead you astray. You’re just immune to it now. Satan is no problem. He just, “Get away from me, Satan. Get back. Get back off.” Not even a struggle for you. See, something’s going on inside of you, deep inside of you. See, that’s God working His work in you. And then the fathers. You see, fathers, you know Him. That’s Jesus from the beginning. You see, now they know God is Jesus. Now they know that Jesus was there at the beginning, to the end of the Bible, and they love Jesus, and they can birth others. See, fathers can birth others through Christ’s gospel. Children can’t birth. See, the father is married. The Bible says that Jesus is our Savior. That’s what babies rely on. But the Bible also says that He’s your Lord. See, are you there? He also says He is your rabbi, your teacher. These guys need to be taught the Word of God. Am I getting this across to you?

See, too many people rely on the Savior stage. The Savior stage is the stage we got to go through. The caterpillar had to be hatched from the egg. It had to be done, but that wasn’t the goal. What was the goal of the egg? A beautiful butterfly. And so we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord. And these young men made Him Lord, so they studied the Word, they took time out for God, they did what God said to do, and they overcame the wicked one. They overcame the world, you see, by the Word of God, and a work was going on in them, transferring them to young adulthood, to fatherhood, into the image of Christ.

chunks.section_question: Can most Christians say what the new covenant is?
chunks.short_answer: He says fathers make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, baby Christians and children by bringing them into the image of Christ. He says over 90% of Christians he asks cannot say what the new covenant is, and asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of, then summarizes the steps: turn from sin, confess it, trust Jesus’s death, burial and resurrection, confess Him as Lord, accept Him, and “I will do all these things.”
chunks.text: Fathers, you know Him, and you can birth others. And this is the image: they birth people in the image of Christ. They make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, out of baby Christians, out of children. They nourish them and they bring them into the image of Christ. Isn’t that powerful? Hallelujah. And that’s the covenant. That’s it, it’s that simple. Most Christians cannot tell me the covenant. Over 90% of them, if I ask them what is the new covenant, they have no idea. How can you live in something that you don’t have knowledge of? How can you inherit things that you have no knowledge of? How can you just be satisfied with just being a saved Christian and not know the promise of the covenant that God promised to you, if you would do these simple things: turn from your sin, confess your sin, put your trust in Jesus’s death, burial, and resurrection, confessing Him as Lord, accept Him in your life? Then He said, “I will do all these things.”

faqs.answer: He says “a covenant is a contract.” He compares it to buying a house, where you promise the lender and the government to pay, “they do their part, I have to do my part,” and says the new covenant is God’s contract with God’s part and ours.

faqs.answer: He says, “depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord.”

faqs.question: What does he say about denominational names on churches?
faqs.answer: He says Paul “plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that putting a name on your church building and saying what you believe “doesn’t count.” He says all of us have the responsibility to line up to Him.

scriptures.text_nkjv: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

faqs.question: Is there another covenant coming after the new covenant?
faqs.answer: No. He says it is the “everlasting” covenant and lists the Adamic, Noah, David and Moses covenants before it: “there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing them good; but I will put My fear in their hearts so that they will not depart from Me.

faqs.question: Why does he say God blesses those who obey His covenant?
faqs.answer: He says God wants to bless your finances, health and life “because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor,” so they see it pays to serve God.

faqs.question: What does he say “repent” means?
faqs.answer: He says “repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways,” leave sin behind, and “believe the gospel.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand. Repent, and believe in the gospel.”

faqs.question: What does he say Luke 13:5 tells us we must do?
faqs.answer: He reads, “Except you repent, you shall all likewise perish,” and says it doesn’t say “except you get baptized” or “except you witness”; “it says except you what? Repent. You turn.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish.”

faqs.question: How does he say we confess our sins?
faqs.answer: He says “I have to admit it with my mouth” and name what is wrong, and then, citing 1 John 1:9, “He is faithful to forgive, and not only forgive, but wash it off, cleanse me of the contamination.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

faqs.question: Does he say a Christian becomes mature right away?
faqs.answer: No. He says “I’m not going to be zapped,” and says old Pentecostals thought “I’m totally mature now,” but “no, no, no,” you go from glory to glory, faith to faith, and salvation to salvation.

faqs.question: How can you tell which stage of Christian growth you are at?
faqs.answer: He says, “you can identify where you’re at today.” If you have habitual sin you are a baby; if you don’t know the doctrines of Christ or believe in your own doctrines, you are a child; if you know the Bible and overcome the wicked one, you are a young man; fathers know Him and can birth others.

scriptures.text_nkjv: I write to you, little children, Because your sins are forgiven you for His name’s sake. I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, Because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, And you have overcome the wicked one.

faqs.question: What does he say about relying only on Jesus as Savior?
faqs.answer: He says “the Savior stage is the stage we got to go through,” like the caterpillar hatching from the egg, “but that wasn’t the goal.” The goal is “a beautiful butterfly,” so we need Jesus as teacher and then as Lord.

faqs.question: How many Christians does he say can tell him what the new covenant is?
faqs.answer: He says “most Christians cannot tell me the covenant,” and over 90% have no idea when he asks, then asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of.
